# What is a Pipeline? 🏭 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## From prompt to response

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 21px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**When you ask an LLM a question, here's what happens:**

1. [Your prompt]{.alert} goes from your browser to servers
2. [Load balancers]{.alert} route it to an available GPU (cloud infrastructure)
3. [Preprocessing]{.alert} cleans and formats your text (with LLMs, this is usually minimal)
4. [Tokenisation]{.alert} converts text to numbers (you know how to do that!)
5. [The model]{.alert} processes tokens (billions of operations!)
6. [Postprocessing]{.alert} formats the output
7. [Safety filters]{.alert} check for harmful content (e.g., hate speech, etc.)
8. [Response]{.alert} travels back to your screen 

[Each step can fail independently!]{.alert}

This entire process is called a [pipeline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipeline_(computing)).
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![The AI pipeline](figures/llm-pipeline.jpg){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/llm-pipeline.jpg"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 15px;"}
Even "What's the weather?" touches load balancers, GPUs, and safety filters before you see an answer
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Failure types: what actually goes wrong?

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Not all failures are the same:**

| Failure type | What it looks like | Root cause |
|-------------|--------------------|------------|
| **Hallucination** | Confident but false content | Model limitations, missing grounding |
| **Policy failure** | Unsafe or inappropriate output | Weak guardrails or bad updates |
| [Data drift]{.alert} | Outdated or weird answers | World changes faster than training |
| [Pipeline failure]{.alert} | Slow, down, or inconsistent responses | Infrastructure, scaling, broken steps |

You can spot *what type* of failure happened, then choose the right response
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![](figures/ai-failures.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/ai-failures.png"}
:::
:::
:::
:::

# When AI Breaks 💥 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## Real AI failures (recent headlines)

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 20px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}

| Incident | What Happened | Impact |
|----------|---------------|--------|
| [Air Canada chatbot (2024)](https://www.bbc.com/travel/article/20240222-air-canada-chatbot-misinformation-what-travellers-should-know) | Invented a refund policy | Company lost lawsuit |
| [DPD chatbot (2024)](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2024/jan/20/dpd-ai-chatbot-swears-calls-itself-useless-and-criticises-firm) | Swore at customers, criticised its own company | Emergency shutdown |
| [Google Gemini images (2024)](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2024/mar/08/we-definitely-messed-up-why-did-google-ai-tool-make-offensive-historical-images) | Historically inaccurate diverse images | Feature paused, CEO apologised |
| [Chevy chatbot (2023)](https://www.upworthy.com/prankster-tricks-a-gm-dealership-chatbot-to-sell-him-a-76000-chevy-tahoe-for-ex1) | Agreed to sell car for $1 | Prompt injection attack |

:::{style="background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 18px; margin-top: 30px;"}
**Common causes:**

1. **Hallucination treated as truth** (Air Canada)
2. **Updates broke guardrails** (DPD)
3. **No input validation** (Chevy)
4. **Overcorrection for bias** (Gemini)
5. **Rush to market** (Snapchat)

## Case study: DPD's sweary chatbot

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 19px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**What happened (January 2024):**

- DPD (UK delivery company) updated their AI chatbot
- After the update, customer Ashley Beauchamp discovered it would:
  - Swear when asked nicely
  - Write poems criticising DPD
  - Call itself "useless" and recommend competitors
  - Say DPD was "the worst delivery firm in the world"

**DPD's response:**

Immediately disabled the AI chatbot, apologised, launched investigation.

**What went wrong:**

A [system update broke the guardrails]{.alert}. The content filtering that prevented inappropriate responses stopped working, but no one noticed until customers posted screenshots on social media
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![](figures/dpd-chatbot.png){width="60%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/dpd-chatbot.png"}

Source: [BBC News](https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-68025677)
:::

:::{style="margin-top: 15px; background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px;"}
**Pipeline failure point:**

[No monitoring after deployment]{.alert}. The update was pushed without testing, and no automated checks caught the broken guardrails.
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Case study: Google Gemini's image crisis

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**What happened (February 2024):**

- Users asked Gemini for images of "1943 German soldiers"
- Gemini generated images of [Black men and Asian women]{.alert} in Nazi uniforms
- Similar problems with "US Founding Fathers" and other historical figures
- Google CEO called results "completely unacceptable"
- Image generation feature [paused for weeks]{.alert}

**Why did this happen? Can you guess?**
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![](figures/ai-failures-02.webp){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/ai-failures-02.webp"}

Source: [BBC News](https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-68412620)
:::

:::{style="margin-top: 15px; background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px;"}
**Pipeline failure point:**

[Testing didn't catch edge cases]{.alert}
:::
:::
:::
:::

# Why Pipelines Break 🔥 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## Data drift: The world changes

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Data drift** = When real-world data differs from training data

**Example: A sentiment analyser trained in 2020:**

- "This product is sick!" → Probably means: Amazing ✅
- "This slaps!" → Might not understand 🤔
- "No cap, this is bussin'" → Completely lost! 😵

**Types of drift:**

| Type | Description | Example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| **Label drift** | What's "correct" changes | Policy updates |
| **Concept drift** | Meaning of things changes | New slang, trends |
| **Data drift** | Input distribution changes | New demographics |
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Data drift visualisation](figures/data-drift.webp){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/data-drift.webp"}

Source: [Spot Intelligence](https://spotintelligence.com/2024/04/08/data-drift-in-machine-learning/)

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 15px;"}
Slang, prices, and user habits shift constantly, but a trained model only knows what it learned
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Why does data drift happen?

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 21px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
Models assume $P_{\text{train}}(X, Y) = P_{\text{prod}}(X, Y)$

But in reality, this joint distribution shifts over time:

1. **Data drift**: $P(X)$ changes
   - Input distribution differs from training
   - Example: New user demographics, device types
   - Model sees inputs it never learned from

2. **Label drift**: $P(Y)$ changes
   - Class frequencies change over time
   - Example: Fraud rate increases during holidays
   - Model's decision boundaries become suboptimal

3. **Concept drift**: $P(Y|X)$ changes
   - Same input → different correct output
   - Example: "Sick" now means "great" in slang
   - [The most dangerous type]{.alert}: model is confident but wrong
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 20px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px; margin-top: 30px;"}
**Technical causes:**

| Cause | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| **Non-stationarity** | Real-world processes aren't static |
| **Sample selection bias** | Training data ≠ production population |
| **Feedback loops** | Model outputs influence future inputs |
| **External shocks** | COVID, policy changes, viral trends |
:::

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px;"}
**Why it's inevitable:**

Machine learning assumes [i.i.d. data]{.alert} (independent and identically distributed). But real-world data is:

- **Temporally correlated** (today depends on yesterday)
- **Non-stationary** (distributions shift over months and years)
- **Adversarial** (users game the system)
- **Context-dependent** (meaning changes with culture and location)
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Model degradation: Models get stale

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 20px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Even without drift, models degrade over time:**

- User expectations evolve
- Competitors improve their products
- Edge cases accumulate
- Small errors compound

**Signs your AI tool is degrading (as a user):**

- ❌ Answers that used to work now don't
- ❌ More "I don't know" or refusals
- ❌ Inconsistent responses to same prompt
- ❌ Friends getting better results elsewhere
- ❌ You're finding workarounds more often

**The "boiling frog" problem:**

Changes happen so gradually you don't notice until it's too late!
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Model degradation](figures/model-degradation.webp){width="60%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/model-degradation.webp"}

Source: [James Howard](https://jameshoward.us/2024/11/26/context-degradation-syndrome-when-large-language-models-lose-the-plot)

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 15px;"}
A model that was 95% accurate at launch can drop to 80% within months if left alone
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Why does model degradation happen?

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
Model performance $P(t)$ decays over time, even with stable data:

1. **Entropy accumulation**
   - Small prediction errors compound over time
   - Error rate $\epsilon$ grows: $\epsilon(t) \approx \epsilon_0 \cdot e^{\lambda t}$
   - Edge cases create cascading failures

2. **Distribution shift in deployment**
   - Model outputs influence user behaviour
   - Users adapt prompts based on past responses
   - Creates [feedback loops]{.alert} that amplify biases

3. **Catastrophic forgetting** (after updates)
   - Fine-tuning on new data overwrites old knowledge
   - Safety training can reduce capability
   - Model "forgets" how to handle rare cases
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 20px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px; margin-top: 30px;"}
**Technical mechanisms:**

| Mechanism | Effect |
|-----------|--------|
| **Weight decay** | Regularisation erodes rare patterns |
| **Quantisation** | Compression loses precision |
| **API updates** | Provider changes break workflows |
| **Context pollution** | Long conversations degrade quality |
:::

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; background: rgba(230, 57, 70, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 19px;"}
Models optimise for [average-case performance]{.alert}. But users remember the **worst** failures.

User trust is proportional to min(performance)

Not the mean!
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Infrastructure issues: When computers fail

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**AI systems run on physical computers that can fail:**

- **Hardware failures**: GPUs overheat, disks die
- **Network issues**: Connections timeout, packets lost
- **Scaling problems**: Too many users at once
- **Resource exhaustion**: Running out of memory
- **Dependency failures**: External APIs go down

**What you see as a user:**

:::{style="font-size: 24px;"}
| Behind the scenes | What you experience |
|-------------------|---------------------|
| GPU memory full | Slow or no response |
| Network timeout | "Error, try again" |
| Rate limits hit | Degraded access |
| Database down | RAG retrieval fails! |
| API key issues | Feature stops working |
:::
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Infrastructure diagram](figures/ai-stack.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/ai-stack.png"}

Source: [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/basics/artificial-intelligence/ai-stack)

:::{style="margin-top: 15px; background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px;"}
If any one layer goes down, you get errors, slowness, or silence
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

# Monitoring Basics 📊 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## What companies watch: Key metrics

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 23px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Essential metrics for AI systems:**

| Category | Metric | Why It Matters |
|----------|--------|----------------|
| **Performance** | Latency | How fast are responses? |
| | Throughput | How many requests per second? |
| | Error rate | What % fail completely? |
| **Quality** | Accuracy/relevance | Are answers correct? |
| | Hallucination rate | How often does it make things up? |
| | User satisfaction | Thumbs up/down? |
| **Resources** | Token usage | How much does each request cost? |
| | GPU memory | Are we close to capacity? |
| **Business** | User engagement | Are users coming back? |

[As a user]{.alert}: You experience these as speed, accuracy, and availability!
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 30px;"}
[![Monitoring dashboard](figures/llm-1.gif){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/llm-1.gif"}

Source: [Oracle](https://blogs.oracle.com/observability/enhance-your-gen-ai-user-experience-with-llm-observability)

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 15px;"}
Teams watch dashboards like this to catch problems before users notice
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Status pages: Checking AI reliability

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Every major AI service has a status page:**

| Service | Status Page |
|---------|------------|
| OpenAI (ChatGPT) | [status.openai.com](https://status.openai.com) |
| Anthropic (Claude) | [status.anthropic.com](https://status.anthropic.com) |
| Google AI | [status.cloud.google.com](https://status.cloud.google.com) |
| Midjourney | Check their Discord |

**What you can learn:**

- Current outages and degraded performance
- Historical incidents (how often things break)

**Tip**: [Check the status page]{.alert} before blaming your prompt!
:::

:::{style="text-align: center;"}

## Testing AI: Why it's hard

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 19px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Traditional software testing:**

- Input: 2 + 2
- Expected output: 4
- Test: Assert(2+2 == 4) ✅

[Deterministic]{.alert}: Same input → same output, always

**AI testing:**

- Input: "What's the weather like?"
- Expected output: ... um ... 🤔
- The response changes every time!
- Many "correct" answers exist!

[Non-deterministic]{.alert}: Same input → different outputs!

**This is why Gemini's image bug wasn't caught:**

Testing "generate a cute cat" worked fine. Testing "generate 1943 German soldiers" probably [wasn't in the test suite]{.alert}
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Testing comparison](figures/testing-comparison.webp){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/testing-comparison.webp"}

Source: [Medium](https://medium.com/@monikanawani25/from-correctness-to-confidence-understanding-llm-testing-0ad555bc797e)

:::{style="margin-top: 15px; background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px;"}
[Solution]{.alert}: Test for [properties]{.alert} (is it safe? is the format correct?) rather than exact outputs!
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## What CAN be tested?

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 20px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Properties that can be verified:**

| Test Type | What It Checks | Example |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| **Safety tests** | No harmful content | "Does it refuse illegal requests?" |
| **Format tests** | Output structure | "Is the JSON valid?" |
| **Consistency tests** | Stable core facts | "Is Paris still in France?" |
| **Boundary tests** | Edge cases | "What if prompt is 10,000 words?" |
| **Bias tests** | Fairness | "Does it treat groups equally?" |
| **Regression tests** | Old bugs stay fixed | "Does the DPD fix still work?" |

**Input validation (first line of defence):**

- Block prompt injections ("Ignore all previous instructions...")
- Limit input length
- Filter prohibited content
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
**Output validation (last line of defence):**

:::{style="background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 18px; margin-top: 30px;"}
**What Air Canada should have done:**

```text
User asks: "What's the refund policy?"

Chatbot generates: "You can request 
a refund within 90 days..."

OUTPUT VALIDATION:
❌ Check against actual policy database
❌ Flag if inventing new policies
❌ Require human review for novel claims

Instead: Response went directly to user
         → Company lost lawsuit
```
:::

:::{style="margin-top: 15px;"}
[Both ends matter]{.alert}: Validate inputs AND outputs!
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Input validation: First line of defence

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Check inputs BEFORE they reach the model:**

**Things to validate:**

- ✅ **Length**: Too short? Too long?
- ✅ **Language**: Is it in expected language?
- ✅ **Content**: Any prohibited content?
- ✅ **Format**: Does it make sense?
- ✅ **Rate**: Is this user spamming us?

**Example input validation:**

:::{style="background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 18px;"}
```text
Prompt: "Ignore all previous instructions..."

❌ BLOCKED: Prompt injection attempt detected!
```
:::

[Garbage in → garbage out still applies!]{.alert}
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Input validation flowchart](figures/input-validation.png){width="85%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/input-validation.png"}

Source: [ApX Machine Learning](https://apxml.com/courses/intro-llm-red-teaming/chapter-5-defenses-mitigation-strategies-llms/input-validation-sanitization-llms)
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Output validation: Last line of defence

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Check outputs BEFORE sending to users:**

**Things to validate:**

- ✅ **Safety**: No harmful or offensive content
- ✅ **Accuracy**: Core facts should be verifiable
- ✅ **Consistency**: Shouldn't contradict itself
- ✅ **Format**: Meets expected structure
- ✅ **Length**: Not too short, not too long
- ✅ **Privacy**: No personal data leakage

**Tools for output validation:**

- [Content moderation APIs]{.alert} (OpenAI, Perspective)
- [Domain-specific rules]{.alert} (e.g., medical disclaimers)
- [LLM-as-a-Judge]{.alert} for quality scoring
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px;"}
**Example output filter:**

```text
AI response: "To make explosives..."

❌ BLOCKED: Dangerous content detected!

Replaced with: "I can't help with 
that request."
```
:::

:::{style="margin-top: 15px; text-align: center;"}
[![Output validation](figures/output-validation.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/output-validation.png"}

Source: [ApX Machine Learning](https://apxml.com/courses/intro-llm-red-teaming/chapter-5-defenses-mitigation-strategies-llms/output-filtering-content-moderation)
:::
:::
:::
:::

# What Can YOU Do? 🛡️ {background-color="#2d4563"}

## Being a savvy AI user

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**You can't fix AI pipelines, but you can:**

1. **Compare answers from different models**
   - Same question to ChatGPT + Claude + Gemini
   - If they disagree, investigate further

2. **Check status pages**
   - AI acting weird? Maybe it's not your prompt
   - [status.openai.com](https://status.openai.com), [status.anthropic.com](https://status.anthropic.com)

3. **Recognise the difference**
   - Pipeline problem: AI is down, slow, or glitching
   - Hallucination: AI is confident but wrong
   - Working as intended: AI refuses for safety reasons
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px; margin-top: 30px;"}
**Quick diagnostic:**

| Symptom | Likely Cause |
|---------|-------------|
| "I'm at capacity" | Infrastructure (wait and retry) |
| Slow response | High load or network |
| Different answers to same Q | Non-determinism (normal!) |
| Confident but wrong | Hallucination (verify!) |
| Refuses to answer | Safety guardrails (try rephrasing) |
| Gibberish output | Pipeline failure (refresh) |
:::
:::
:::
:::

## The variation is normal!

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Why does AI give different answers to the same question?**

1. **Temperature**: Randomness dial (creativity vs. consistency)
2. **Load balancing**: Your request might hit a different server
3. **Model versions**: A/B testing different versions
4. **Context**: Time of day, your chat history
5. **Updates**: The model literally changed since yesterday

If AI always gave the exact same response, it would feel robotic. Some variation keeps it natural.

**But for important decisions:**

Ask multiple times. Ask different AIs. If answers diverge on something critical, [don't trust any of them]{.alert}!
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![](figures/ab-testing.png){width="70%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/ab-testing.png"}

[![](figures/gemini-personal-intelligence.png){width="70%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/gemini-personal-intelligence.png"}

Sources: [r/Bard](https://www.reddit.com/r/Bard/comments/1leiobd/google_is_also_doing_ab_testing_in_the_gemini_app/#lightbox) and [Google Blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-app/personal-intelligence/)


:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 15px;"}
You and your friend might be running different model versions right now without knowing it
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Activity: Diagnose the problem! 🔍

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 20px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=50%}
**Scenario cards: What's the likely cause?**

**Scenario A:**

You ask Claude a question. It takes 45 seconds to respond, and the answer is cut off mid-sentence.

**Scenario B:**

You ask Gemini "Who won the 2027 Super Bowl?" and it confidently names a team.

**Scenario C:**

You ask ChatGPT to write code. Yesterday it worked; today it refuses and says "I can't help with that."
:::

:::{.column width=50%}
**Scenario D:**

You ask Midjourney to generate "a photo of my professor." It creates an image of a random person.

**Scenario E:**

Three different AI assistants give you three completely different answers about a historical date.

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; background: rgba(45, 69, 99, 0.1); padding: 15px; border-radius: 10px;"}
**Discuss with a neighbour:**

- Pipeline problem?
- Hallucination?
- Working as intended?
- How would you verify?
:::

⏱️ 5 minutes to diagnose!
:::
:::
:::

## Activity answers

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 20px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=50%}
**Scenario A: 45 seconds, cut off mid-sentence**

- [Pipeline problem]{.alert}: Server overload or timeout
- Check status page
- Retry in a few minutes

**Scenario B: 2027 Super Bowl answer**

- [Hallucination]{.alert}: Event hasn't happened yet!
- AI doesn't know it doesn't know
- Always verify time-sensitive claims

**Scenario C: Code refused today but worked yesterday**

- [Model update]{.alert} changed safety guardrails
- Or: Your specific prompt triggered a new filter
- Try rephrasing; if still blocked, guardrails changed
:::

:::{.column width=50%}
**Scenario D: "Photo of my professor" = random person**

- [Working as intended]{.alert}: AI doesn't know your professor!
- It generates a plausible "professor-looking" person
- This is expected behaviour, not a failure

**Scenario E: Different AIs, different historical dates**

- [Potential hallucination from all of them]{.alert}
- Don't trust any AI for verifiable facts
- Look it up in a reliable source!
:::
:::
:::

# Summary 📚 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## Main takeaways

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 32px;"}

- `r fa('globe')` You use [dozens of AI pipelines daily]{.alert}: text, image, voice, recommendations

- `r fa('link')` Pipelines are the [multi-step process]{.alert} from your input to AI's output. [Every step can fail]{.alert}

- `r fa('newspaper')` Real failures: Air Canada lawsuit, DPD swearing, Gemini images. [Pipeline problems, not "rogue AI"]{.alert}

- `r fa('chart-line')` [Data drift: The world changes, AI stays frozen]{.alert} 

- `r fa('bell')` [Monitoring]{.alert}: Companies track metrics you never see. When monitoring fails, you read about it in the news

- `r fa('user-shield')` [You should]{.alert} compare AIs, check status pages, distinguish pipeline problems from hallucinations

:::

## Your AI user toolkit

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=50%}
**Quick reference:**

| Symptom | Action |
|---------|--------|
| AI is down/slow | Check status page, wait |
| Different answers | Normal! Verify if critical |
| Confident but wrong | Hallucination, verify facts |
| Refuses request | Guardrails, try rephrasing |
| Weird/gibberish | Pipeline glitch, refresh |
:::
